texto: When we replace the names with pronouns, the accusative (usually the neutral pronoun **es** or **ihn/sie**) goes immediately before the dative: **Ich gebe es ihm** (I give it to him), **Kannst du es mir zeigen?** (can you show it to me?).
Compare with attention: With two nouns: **Ich gebe meinem Bruder (Dat.) das Buch (Akk.)**. With two pronouns: **Ich gebe es (Akk.) ihm (Dat.)**. You never say «ich gebe ihm es»!

filas: Ich gebe dem Freund das Buch.
Sie schenkt der Mutter die Blumen.
Kannst du mir das Foto zeigen?
Er schickt dem Chef die E-Mail.

frases.en: Have you seen my German book?

frases.de: Ja, du hast es mir gestern geliehen.
frases.en: Yeah, you lent it to me yesterday.

frases.de: Brauchst du es noch für den Unterricht?
frases.en: You still need it for class?

frases.de: Nein, ich gebe es dir heute wieder.
frases.en: No, I'll give it back to you today.

bloques.pregunta: When both supplements are personal pronouns, what is the correct order?

opciones.explicacion: With pronouns, the fixed rule requires to place the accusative before the dative (is ihm / es mir).
This order applies when both supplements are substantive, not pronouns.
«ich gebe ihm es» is not grammatically correct in standard German.

bloques.pregunta: How is «Can you explain?» correctly translated into German?

opciones.explicacion: Neutral acusative (s) before the dative (mir): is mir.
The accuser must precede the dative when both are pronouns.
The addressee requires a dative (mir), not an accusative (mich).

bloques.frase: Hast du das Buch? Ja, ich gebe ___ morgen wieder.

opciones.explicacion: Reverse the mandatory order of the two pronouns.
«dich» is accusative; the recipient requires dative (dir).
The accusative pronoun (s) is preponderated to the dative (mir).
Wrong order: the dative cannot precede the accusative pronoun.
«mich» is accusative; the person to whom something is shown goes in dative (mir).

bloques.frase: Ich habe das Buch und gebe es ihm.

opciones.texto: I've received the letter and I give it to him.
opciones.explicacion: gebe is ihm = I give it to him (accusative is + dative ihm).

opciones.texto: He gave the letter to me.
opciones.explicacion: The subject is «ich» and the person who receives is «ihm».

opciones.texto: I sent a letter to my friend yesterday.
opciones.explicacion: It does not match the text or the pronouns of the phrase.

bloques.frase: Julia braucht das Buch. Tim schenkt ___ zum Geburtstag.

opciones.explicacion: Neutral accused (s) before the date (ihr = to it).
The order of pronouns requires an accusative before the date.

bloques.explicacion: It is before the tativa mir.

intro: If the two supplements of a sentence are personal pronouns, the rule is completely reversed with respect to the nouns: the pronoun in **acusativo precede siempre al dativo** («es mir», «es ihm»).
